A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Q-DiT4SR and support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures. All 11 pages of v3 and 12 pages of v4 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v3 reports original super-resolution evaluations on four datasets, quantitative ablations in Tables 2–4, and visual and activation analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds runtime measurements, DreamClear evaluation, calibration robustness tests, and local artifact analysis in Tables 5–9.

M1.justification: H-SVD, VaSMP, VaTMP, and their quantization and scheduling procedures remain unchanged. The new execution details document implementation, and Section 4.5 explicitly applies the same framework to DreamClear without backbone-specific modification.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds DIV2K calibration data and calibration-transfer scenarios using DrealSR and DIV2K instead of RealSR. The four existing evaluation datasets and super-resolution task remain unchanged; DreamClear adds a backbone rather than a dataset or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained benchmark comparisons and ablations is unchanged. The new runtime comparisons reuse FP and SVDQuant, while the local artifact study reuses existing component variants; no new competing quantization method is introduced.

E3.justification: v4 adds several evaluation protocols: W4A4 profiling with batch size 16 on a reported RTX-4090 48GB GPU, DreamClear configurations, alternative 32-image calibration sets, and targeted 64×64 regions from 32 randomly selected RealSR images. The local study introduces ROI-PSNR, Edge MAE, and Color MAE. These are new experiments; the original benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and rank ablations, v4 tests sensitivity to calibration domain and quantifies local fidelity, edge, and color artifacts across component combinations in Tables 8–9. DreamClear generalization and the component runtime breakdown further expand analysis of applicability and deployment bottlenecks.

E5.justification: The new tables continue point-estimate reporting without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing variance plots are unchanged; the newly specified image counts describe evaluation samples, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values, while Tables 5–9 add substantial results on efficiency, DreamClear, calibration robustness, and artifacts. Table 6 reports FP/Q-DiT4SR latency of 3099.30/686.50 ms, or 4.51× speedup. Table 9 reports baseline/full-method ROI-PSNR of 19.6684/20.9590. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements to the retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–23, Gaussian and high-rate assumptions, hierarchical decomposition, distortion reasoning, and bit-allocation mathematics are unchanged. The added empirical metrics and implementation discussion introduce no new formal definitions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same novelty, detail-preservation, mixed-precision, and W4A6/W4A4 performance claims. The stated 5.8× model-size and 6.14× operation reductions are unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 4.4–4.6 add explanations of runtime bottlenecks, a cautious perceptual-regularization hypothesis for DreamClear, calibration-domain stability, and weight-versus-activation sources of artifacts. New limitations identify difficult thin, repetitive, and high-contrast textures and qualify deployment claims because native arbitrary-precision kernels are unsupported. The earlier general warning about no-reference IQA metrics is retained.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands deployment documentation: parallel execution of SVD-G with the quantized branch, a Triton implementation of SVD-L avoiding dense reconstruction, and mapping mixed-precision schedules to standard low-bit computations. It also supplies profiling hardware and batch size and local-study sampling details. These are newly documented details, not established changes to the earlier implementation; the code/model release promise remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for NTIRE 2017/DIV2K, Pixelated Butterfly, Scatterbrain, and Monarch, and explains implementation connections to Nunchaku and structured matrices. The IMPQ-to-CoopQ update concerns the same cited arXiv identifier, 2509.15455, rather than a newly introduced work. Overall novelty positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The document adds Sections 4.4–4.6, acknowledgments, and an impact statement, and replaces the preprint notice with conference publication text. These are localized structural additions; the existing introduction, method exposition, results discussion, and conclusion receive little rewriting.

P2.justification: Five new tables substantially expand the quantitative presentation, separately displaying practical efficiency, runtime components, DreamClear results, calibration robustness, and local artifacts. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–4 are retained, while the inserted displays reflow the closing sections and references.

improvement.justification: v3 supports deployment chiefly through parameter and operation counts. v4 adds measured memory and latency, including the modest efficiency penalty relative to SVDQuant, and strengthens generality and detail-preservation evidence through Tables 7–9. These additions address important validation gaps, while explicit artifact and kernel-support limitations improve transparency. Exact precision mapping and statistical uncertainty remain insufficiently documented, but the overall evidential improvement is substantial.
